newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks snap eight-day winning streak.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks snap eight-day winning streak.

text.p: Colombian stocks snapped an eight-day winning streak and ended mostly lower as profit-taking took some of the shine off blue-chips such as brewer Bavaria that have performed strongly since the start of the year.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index slipped 0.42 percent to close at 17,113.56 on above-average trading volume of more than 6.5 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB fell 0.72 percent, meanhile, ending at 1,122.28 on active trading of about 3.7 billion pesos.
Bavaria, flagship of the Julio Mario Santo Domingo conglomerate, accounted for nearly 1 billion pesos of total volume in Bogota.

The company's stock, which posted one of its first losses of the year Thursday, extended its losses in Bogota Friday by falling an added 2.93 percent. The drop came on follow-through selling after authoritative denials of rumors that Brazil's Companhia Cervejaria Brahma was considering buying a stake in Bavaria, brokers said.
"The offer selling of Bavaria shares couldn't be stopped and I think it will see an even bigger correction due to the high valuation it reached," one Bogota-based broker said.
Banks were also hit by profit-taking with Banco de Bogota falling 1.10 percent in Bogota to end at 6,101 pesos per share.
In Medellin, losers were led by Bancoquia, which was heavily traded and dropped 3.08 percent to close at 3,150 pesos a share.
The day's few winners included firms belonging to the Medellin-based Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group, a favorite among foreign investment funds.

Sueramericana de Seguros, crown jewel of the group and Colombia's largest insurer, ended up 1.20 percent in Medellin at 25,300 per share. Compania de Cementos Argos, another winner among the group's diversified holdings, closed up 0.90 percent in Bogota at 7,951 pesos per share.
